## Map {#sec-map-documentation}

::: {.content-visible when-format="html"}
{{< skeleton-viz map >}}
:::

### `Map(UF)`
Creates a `Map` instance with the supplied user function.

```cpp
#include <skepu>

int sum(int a, int b)
{
    return a + b;
}

int main()
{
    auto vsum = skepu::Map(sum);
}
```

### `operator()`
Calls the `Map` instance, performing the user function on the input parameters, and stores the result in the output containers. Below is an example with one output `Vector`, two input `Vector`s, one proxy `Vec`, and one scalar. 

```{.cpp .run}
#include <skepu>
#include <skepu-lib/io.hpp>

int sum(int a, int b, skepu::Vec<int> v, int c)
{
    return a + b + v(0) + v(1) + c;
}

int main()
{
    skepu::Vector<int> a{1, 2, 3, 4}, b{4, 3, 2, 1}, v{1, 2};
    skepu::Vector<int> out(a.size());

    auto vsum = skepu::Map(sum);
    vsum(out, a, b, v, 10);
    skepu::io::cout << out << "\n";
}
```

```{.text .output}
Vector[4]: 18 18 18 18
```

### `setStride(int...)`
Sets the stride of the output and input containers of the `Map` instance. All strides are set to 1 by default.

```{.cpp .run}
#include <skepu>
#include <skepu-lib/io.hpp>

skepu::multiple<int, int> mult(int a, int b)
{
    return skepu::ret(a * b, a * b);
}

int main()
{
    skepu::Vector<int> a{1, 2, 3, 4}, b{2, 2};
    skepu::Vector<int> out1(b.size() * 4), out2(b.size() * 6);

    auto vsum = skepu::Map(mult);
    vsum.setStride(4, 6, 2, 1);
    vsum(out1, out2, a, b);
    skepu::io::cout << out1 << "\n";
    skepu::io::cout << out2 << "\n";
}
```

```{.text .output}
Vector[8]: 2 0 0 0 6 0 0 0
Vector[12]: 2 0 0 0 0 0 6 0 0 0 0 0
```
